newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SEEDS SENT PACKING AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SEEDS SENT PACKING AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Former champion Mary Pierce and unheralded American Kimberly Po swept aside seeded rivals on Sunday to advance to the quarter-finals of the Australian Open on a day of surprises at Melbourne Park.

Last year's finalist Anke Huber of Germany, the fifth seed, became the first victim, crashing to Pierce. She was quickly followed to the locker room by American seventh seed Lindsay Davenport who fell to compatriot Po.
In the men's draw, Spain's Carlos Moya produced yet more stunning baseline tennis on Sunday to oust fellow non-seed Jonas Bjorkman of Sweden for a quarter-final place.
Moya, world-ranked 25th, bundled German defending champion Boris Becker out of the tournament in the first round and has continued to woo the Melbourne crowd.

Pierce, who has slipped to 22 in the world rankings after reaching number three two years ago, played with typical slowness between points against Huber, receiving a warning from the chair umpire on her way to a 6-2 6-3 victory.

The Florida-based right-hander has dropped only one set in her opening four matches and is displaying the same athleticism which carried her to glory at the Australian Open in 1995, when she also beat Huber in the fourth round.

"I was thinking a little bit last night about two years ago when I played her (Huber) in the same round, but every match and every tournament is different and this match was certainly different," said Pierce.
Seventh-ranked Huber battled to find the target against Pierce with her serve, dropping three service games in the opening set and double-faulting five times in the match.
"She played very deep and long, so it was very hard for me to find my rhythm and play my game," said Huber, whose preparation for the Open has been affected by injuries.
Huber, who lost to Monica Seles in last year's final at Melbourne Park, said she had been a prepared for Pierce's notoriously slow rate of play.
"But she takes a lot of time and you can still feel crazy on the other side of the net," she said.
Pierce will play either Spanish third seed Conchita Martinez or 16th seed Sabine Appelmans of Belgium in the quarter-finals.
Davenport, world ranked number nine, has never lived up to expectations in the big tournaments failing to advance beyond the quarter-finals in 18 previous Grand Slam events.
Unseeded Po, ranked number 23 in the world, produced her best result in 19 Grand Slams to upstage Davenport 7-6 6-4 in 95 minutes.
It was an evenly-balanced and at times scrappy match. Po only won the first set after a marathon 15-13 tie-break and proved the most committed and consistent of the two in the second set.

Unseeded Spaniard Moya, a 20-year-old who was until recently considered a clay court specialist, took an early lead against Bjorkman but fell two sets to one down as the serve-and-volley specialist came forward to dominate from the net.
Helped by a steadily-improving serve, Moya rallied to win the match 6-3 1-6 3-6 6-2 6-4 with a succession of unreturnable backhands and forehands.
He served 10 aces in a match lasting two hours and 27 minutes.
Moya, one of three Spanish men who started the fourth round, will meet either compatriot Felix Mantilla, the men's 14th seed, or American MaliVai Washington in the quarter-finals.
